hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive gain).
Response lags command by tens of seconds and settles over several minutes, not instantly.
There is negligible dead-zone: u=0.2-0.5 produces a clear rise from current y.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient low values.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across input levels.
Steady-state input needed to hold target y=0.5 is in mid-range ~0.4-0.6.
Sensor noise is small (<0.01) relative to control band width 0.05.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in response direction, magnitude/gain and lag at mid-power, which is required to estimate steady-state input for target and to choose controller gain and timing.
proposal.safety_argument: Starting from y=0.2482, worst-case bound is 0.2482+0.006*0.5*180=0.7882 which is below soft limit 0.85 with margin, and well below hard cutoff 0.9; actual rise will be lower due to heat loss and lag.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y should start near 0.25, rise after a short lag with positive slope, reaching roughly 0.4-0.6 by end of 180s with slope flattening if approaching equilibrium.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero completed experiments so no uncertainties are resolved; gain, lag, zero-decay, linearity, steady-state for target, and noise all remain unmeasured and controller cannot be justified.
proposal.operator_note: First probe: hold mid-power 0.5 for 180 s to measure direction, rate and lag.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in settled gain/equilibrium at u=0.5 and settling time by extending the same hold until slope flattens, which is required to estimate steady-state input for target.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.5387 + 0.006*0.5*90 = 0.8087 stays below soft limit 0.85 with margin, using no-decay no-lag assumption.
proposal.expected_observation: If heater has first-order lag with equilibrium above current y, y should continue rising from ~0.54 toward ~0.60-0.68 over 90s with slope declining from 0.002/s toward flattening; if slope stays ~0.002/s then equilibrium is still far above and time constant is longer.
proposal.readiness_justification: Only one amplitude tested and equilibrium not reached (slope 0.002/s at end of E1); still need second amplitude/linearity, controlled decay at u=0 with time constant, settled gain for target, and noise quantification before controller design, so not ready.
proposal.operator_note: Holding half power longer to see if temperature levels off near target.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in zero-input decay, ambient equilibrium, and cooling time constant, which is required to choose holding power and controller timing.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound is 0.6397 + 0.006*0.0*480 = 0.6397, well below soft limit 0.85 with no possible rise at u=0.

proposal.readiness_justification: Only 2 experiments completed so readiness requires at least 3; gain at u=0.5 and ~270s settling are becoming clear but zero-decay rate, second gain point for linearity, and noise magnitude remain unresolved and are needed for controller design.
proposal.operator_note: Holding at zero power to measure natural cooldown and ambient level.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Tests intermediate gain/linearity and steady-state power for y=0.5 by holding predicted u~0.35 from low y, distinguishing linear-interpolated H6 from dead-zone/nonlinear alternatives, which is required to choose feedforward and gain for controller.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound using trusted formula: 0.1821 + 0.006*0.35*300 = 0.8121, which stays below soft limit 0.85 and hard cutoff 0.9; real rise will be smaller due to heat loss seen in E3.
proposal.expected_observation: If positive-gain linear hypothesis with tau ~150-200s is right, y should rise from ~0.18 after short lag at ~0.001-0.002/s, reaching ~0.40-0.50 by end of 300s with slope declining as it approaches equilibrium near 0.5; flat response would indicate dead-zone, overshoot past 0.6 would indicate larger gain.
proposal.readiness_justification: H1 direction, H2 multi-minute lag, and H4 decay to ~0.2 are well supported by E1-E3, but H5 linearity has only two settled points (u=0 and u=0.5), H6 holding input ~0.34 is interpolated not directly observed, H3 dead-zone is untested at low u, and noise looks ~0.02-0.05 comparable to band; one intermediate hold is needed before controller design, so not ready.
proposal.operator_note: Holding at 0.35 power for 300 s from cold to check power needed for target.

proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound per trusted model: 0.5011 + 0.006*0.35*150 = 0.816 < soft limit 0.85; true rise limited further by approaching equilibrium near 0.5 and heat loss, so margin ~0.034.
proposal.expected_observation: If first-order heater with tau ~150-200s and eq ~0.51-0.53 at u=0.35 is right, y should stay near 0.50-0.53 over 150s with slope decaying from 0.0012/s toward ~0; continued rise above 0.55 would indicate larger gain, flat/decay would indicate lower eq.
proposal.readiness_justification: Gain direction, cooling to ~0.2, lag of minutes, and linearity (~0.9 gain) are resolved; steady-state power narrowed to ~0.32-0.35 but not resolved because E4 slope 0.0012 shows equilibrium not yet reached, so feedforward within band cannot be fixed yet - one same-command hold to settle is needed before controller design.
proposal.operator_note: Holding power at 35% a little longer to see if temperature settles at target.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in steady-state input for y=0.5 and local gain/linearity near target by testing u=0.30 from above, which directly sets feedforward and integrator needs for control.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.5495 + 0.006*0.30*150 = 0.8195 stays below soft limit 0.85 with margin, using current y 0.5495.
proposal.expected_observation: If eq at u=0.35 is >0.55 and eq at u=0.5 is ~0.65, then u=0.30 eq should be ~0.46-0.51; starting from ~0.55 y should decay slowly toward/into band top over 150s at ~-0.0005 to -0.001/s with +/-0.02 noise; flat/rise would indicate 0.30 eq >=0.55 and linear model wrong.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, ambient ~0.19, and multi-minute lag are resolved; but exact feedforward for 0.5 is not: E4 reached 0.498 rising at 0.35 and E5 rose to 0.55 still rising, so 0.35 is too high by unknown 0.02-0.05 which exceeds band half-width 0.025, plus noise ~0.02-0.05 needs a settle-from-above test before fixing controller gain/integral.
proposal.operator_note: Holding 0.30 power for 150s from above band to bracket the feedforward that holds 0.50.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Narrows steady-state feedforward for y=0.5 and local gain near target from u=0.30 holding just above band, which directly sets feedforward and integrator needs for the controller.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.5339 + 0.006*0.28*180 = 0.836 stays below soft limit 0.85 and hard cutoff 0.9 with no decay or lag assumed.
proposal.expected_observation: Starting ~0.534, y should decay slowly toward 0.49-0.52 over 180s at about -0.0002 to -0.0006/s with +/-0.02 noise; end mean ~0.50-0.53 with slope near zero if eq is ~0.50. Flat at ~0.53 would mean eq at 0.28 is still above target and feedforward must be lower.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, lag over minutes, ambient decay, and large noise are resolved enough for control structure, but steady-state feedforward is not yet centered: E6 shows u=0.30 holds 0.531 flat just above band top 0.525 and E5 shows u=0.35 rising past 0.55, so 0.27-0.30 remains to be confirmed with one small step down before integrator and gains can be fixed.
proposal.operator_note: Holding just below current power to see if temperature settles inside the target band.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive gain).
Response lags command and settles over several minutes (tau ~150-250s, settle ~300-450s), not instantly.
There is no dead-zone in tested 0.28-0.5 range: u>=0.28 produces clear heating/hold; behavior below u=0.2 is untested.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient ~0.15-0.20.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear across all input levels globally.
Steady-state input needed to hold target y=0.5 is ~0.27-0.29; u=0.28 holds ~0.506 in-band, u=0.30 holds ~0.531 just above band, u=0.35 holds >0.55.
Sensor noise is ~0.01-0.02 RMS with occasional 0.03-0.05 outliers, comparable to band half-width 0.025, not <0.01.
Change is weaker actuator: same u gives smaller heating rise and lower held level, but u=0 cooling rate/delay/ambient and sensor calibration/noise are unchanged from E3/E6-E7.
Change is faster outflow/heat loss: fall at u=0 is faster/steeper than E3 and same u holds lower level, with similar delay and sensor behaviour.
Change is slower response: transport delay is much longer than ~20s and/or heating/cooling time constant is much longer, while steady-state gain and sensor are unchanged.
Change is sensor shift: true thermal dynamics/gain are unchanged but reading has new offset and/or changed noise, so apparent 0.45 level at u~0.30-0.42 does not reflect true temperature.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in post-change delay, u=0 cooling rate/ambient, and sensor offset/noise, which discriminates weaker actuator (same cooling as E3) vs faster outflow (faster fall) vs slower response (longer flat/slower fall) vs sensor (shifted ambient/changed noise) and sets timing and feedforward for revised control.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case rise is current y + RATE*u*duration = 0.4582 + 0.006*0*480 = 0.4582, well below soft limit 0.85; u=0 cannot rise and is safe at any duration.
proposal.expected_observation: If baseline delay/cooling unchanged (weaker-actuator leading case), y should hold ~0.45-0.48 for ~15-25 s after switch (still responding to prior ~0.42 in-transit command), then fall with E3-like slope toward ~0.20-0.25 by end of 480 s; much faster/steeper fall implies faster outflow, much longer flat (>50 s) or much slower fall implies slower response/delay increase, same shape but shifted ambient/noise change implies sensor offset/noise change.
proposal.readiness_justification: Not ready: monitoring shows same u now holds ~0.05-0.08 lower with flat response to +0.12 u ramp, consistent with C1/C2/C3 and partly C4, but with zero after-change experiments delay, cooling slope, ambient, and noise shift are unresolved; one draining hold is needed before designing controller.
proposal.operator_note: Draining at u=0 from 0.46 to measure delay and cooling rate to separate gain, loss, lag, and sensor changes.

proposal.safety_argument: Current y=0.1713; worst-case rise 0.1713+0.006*0.35*300=0.801 below 0.85 soft limit with ~0.05 margin and ~0.10 to hard 0.9; prior 480s hold at u=0 means no high command in transit to add; starting from near-ambient low level.

proposal.readiness_justification: Delay greatly increased and large sensor-noise change are largely ruled out by E8 prompt fall within ~16s and similar noise/ambient, but heating gain vs loss rate remains ambiguous because u=0 cooling comparison is confounded by different start level and in-transit prior command; one comparable heating hold from low level is needed to measure initial slope vs plateau before designing feedforward/gain.
proposal.operator_note: Holding 0.35 from low level to compare heating slope and plateau to E4.

proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case conservative rise 0.3696 + 0.006*0.6*120 = 0.8016 stays below 0.85 soft limit with no decay/lag assumed, starting from low 0.37; 120s at 0.6 cannot reach soft limit even if gain were baseline.

proposal.operator_note: Probing high-power heating slope from current low level to separate weaker heater from faster loss and estimate new feedforward.

submission.machine_card: Heater, positive gain. u=0 decays to ambient ~0.15-0.20 (E3 0.66->0.18 in 480s). u=0.28 holds ~0.506 in-band (E7), u=0.30 holds ~0.531 just above band (E6), u=0.35 holds >0.55 still rising (E5), u=0.5 holds ~0.65 (E2). Local gain ~0.8-1.25 (0.02u ->0.025y between E6/E7; global (0.647-0.17)/0.5~0.95). Lag dominant: tau heating ~150s (E1 0.21->0.53 in 180s), cooling ~210s (E3), settle 300-450s, no instant jump. No dead-zone in 0.28-0.5; below 0.2 untested. Self-draining on its own. Noise ~0.01-0.02 RMS with 0.03-0.05 outliers, comparable to band half-width 0.025. Rate bound 0.006/unit/s. Keep steady duty ~0.27-0.29 for 0.5.
submission.design_rationale: First-order heater tau~150-210s, K~1.0-1.2, ambient~0.175. Feedforward uff=(target-0.175)/1.15 gives 0.283 at 0.5, matching measured E7 0.28->0.506 and E6 0.30->0.531. PI trims residual: Kp=0.9 gives loop gain ~1, closed-loop tau~85s without amplifying 0.01-0.02 noise; Ki=0.008 (Ti~112s) removes offset inside 300s settling. EMA Tf=12s + outlier de-weighting suppresses noise vs 0.025 half-band. Integration enabled only when |e|<0.15 and yf<0.70 plus saturation back-calculation to avoid heat-up windup from 0.3 errors, while limits [-0.18,+0.22] leave >0.16 authority to correct feedforward error. Output clamp [0,0.75] and yf>0.75 cutback plus 2.5s output smoothing keep far from 0.85/0.9 limits and minimize u^2 dither.
submission.predicted_behavior: From cold 0.2, u~0.55 then backs to ~0.37 at 0.4, reaches band in ~130-170s without overshoot, settles inside band by ~200-250s. From hot 0.7, u~0.1 cools to band in ~150s. Steady dither +/-0.005 in u, y filtered +/-0.006, >85% time in band after 300s, MAE ~0.008-0.012, steady duty ~0.27-0.30. No 0.85 exceedance, no override.

Expanded IMAX+UMAX guarantees reachability even before bias learns; coordinated anti-windup prevents double-integrator windup; filter/slew/safety unchanged because noise/delay/sensor unchanged.

submission.design_rationale: First-order heater y_dot=(K*u-(y-AMB))/tau. Pre-change: AMB~0.175, K~1.15, u_ss(0.5)~0.28, tau~200s, delay ~15-20s. submission.design_rationale: Actuator-weaker needs larger steady-state u, not faster cooling or more delay. Estimating Kobs=(yavg-AMB)/uavg when settled directly identifies the new K and moves ff to (target-AMB)/Kest, while scheduling KP,KI by K_nom/Kest keeps KP*K and KI*K ~constant so nominal phase margin is preserved and degraded response is not sluggish/oscillatory. Gating on settledness and saturation prevents learning transients/noise; starting from nominal K preserves nominal in-band >0.94 and allows upward adaptation only on evidence.
